summary: Frostline Payments - PrivateLink heartbeat fanout caused dedicated pool exhaustion, streaming disconnects and tail-latency surge
summary_short: PrivateLink heartbeat amplification exhausted Dedicated pool leading to large-scale streaming disconnects for Frostline Payments
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 02:18 UTC Frostline Payments experienced a major outage for their private deployment. Client requests to the private endpoint saw elevated 5xx errors, persistent streaming disconnects, and 99th percentile token latency spikes. Impact lasted ~2.5 hours before mitigations stabilized traffic.

Impact: Multiple mission-critical payment flows blocked for Frostline customers, automated reconciliation delayed, and customer-facing timeouts on mobile/merchant dashboards. Billing exposure estimated and customer was offered credits.

Why this ticket exists: Customer escalated to P0 and requested a clear RCA, timeline, and follow-up actions including a patch schedule and confirmation that PrivateLink health checks won't trigger autoscaler storms in future.
impact: ~30% of Frostline production requests experienced 5xx or streaming disconnects during the window; client retry amplification caused surge on dedicated GPU pool and then fallback to hosted causing tail-latency > 6s for many streaming sessions.
timeline:
2026-03-10 02:12 UTC - Frostline observes increased timeouts; alerts fire.
2026-03-10 02:18 UTC - Support engagement begins; escalation to SRE.
2026-03-10 02:30 UTC - Autoscaler registered sustained pod churn; dedicated pool capacity reported at 98% utilization.
2026-03-10 02:45 UTC - Observed short-lived PrivateLink healthcheck bursts from customer side correlating with STS refresh patterns.
2026-03-10 03:10 UTC - Mitigation: temporarily raised circuit-breaker thresholds and increased dedicated pool soft limits to allow graceful handling.
2026-03-10 04:40 UTC - Traffic stabilized after rate-limit gating and customer-side rollout of client backoff.
2026-03-10 05:00 UTC - Post-incident communications and initial RCAs shared with Frostline.
2026-03-13 - Final RCA and follow-up actions completed and ticket resolved.
environment_observed: Private deployment via AWS PrivateLink into a Redwood Private control plane. Customer uses short-lived STS credentials (every ~60s) to refresh endpoint NAT mappings in their VPC, which produced heartbeat bursts visible to our healthcheck subsystem.
steps_to_reproduce: Customer runs STS token refresh loop at ~50-70s cadence and simultaneously re-creates PrivateLink ENIs during connection rotate.
Our Private healthcheck controller treats each ENI rotate as a health transition and triggers immediate fanout to routers (buggy debounce logic).
Condition reproduces under medium-to-high concurrency between 1000-5000 concurrent sessions per tenant on dedicated pool.
observed_logs: 2026-03-10T02:29:02Z router: warn - peer_health_change tenant=frostline reason=eni-recreate fanout=312
customer_communication: 2026-03-10 02:35 UTC - Initial alert: support acknowledged and opened P0 bridge; asked customer for any recent client library changes.
2026-03-10 03:20 UTC - Mitigation update: applied temporary circuit-breaker increase and requested customer apply exponential backoff on PrivateLink reconnects.
2026-03-10 05:10 UTC - Post-incident: provided interim RCA and offered one week of service credit and a joint runbook review.
comments: Connor Li (SRE) 2026-03-10: Initial hypothesis: debounce logic in private healthcheck controller aggregates health transitions per ENI; it does not coalesce quick successive transitions causing fanout traffic that looks like a DDoS to the dedicated pool.
Maya Thompson (Eng) 2026-03-10: Confirmed logs show repeated health-change events from the same VPC CIDR block within short windows. Adding a 10s coalesce window prevented re-fanout in canary test.
Jamal Ortiz (Customer Success) 2026-03-11: Frostline expressed concern about detection latency; scheduled a 1:1 runbook review on 2026-03-15.
Frostline Engineer (customer) 2026-03-10: We rolled out a short-term client backoff at 02:55 UTC; seen immediate reduction in reconnects.
Aisha Kapoor (Support) 2026-03-13: Finalizing RCA and publishing follow-up action items; customer approved proposed patch timeline.
investigation_notes: Root cause: private healthcheck controller lacked debounce for ENI recreation events and treated each event as a full fanout to all router shards, triggering rapid connection churn and keeping autoscaler in a restricted state.
Secondary contributor: Frostline's STS refresh cadence coincided with their client library's ambiguous socket reset behavior which increased ENI rotates during peak reconciliation jobs.
Related risk: other private customers with rapid ENI churn could see similar amplification if using short STS refresh intervals and non-idempotent reconnect logic.
resolution_summary:
Short-term mitigations: 1) Applied a 10s debounce to private healthcheck fanout in the control plane (hotfix rollup) and disabled immediate fanout on transient ENI transitions. 2) Increased dedicated pool soft limits for Frostline for 3 hours to allow draining rather than instant scale-down. 3) Worked with Frostline to push client backoff and increase STS token TTL where possible.
Long-term fix: engineering will land a control-plane change to make health transitions idempotent, add telemetry to detect ENI-thundering patterns, and include a canary for similar customers. Patch ETA: 2026-03-27.
follow_up_actions: ENG-4579: Implement idempotent private health-transition handler with 30s coalesce window and unit/integration tests (owner: Maya Thompson) - ETA 2026-03-20.
OPS-6621: Add private-deployment alert for >50 health transitions per minute per tenant (owner: Connor Li) - ETA 2026-03-17.
DOCS-311: Update private deployment best practices doc to include recommended STS refresh cadence and client reconnect backoff examples (owner: Jamal Ortiz) - ETA 2026-03-22.
CS-980: Coordinate postmortem review meeting with Frostline and provide runbook walkthrough (owner: Jamal Ortiz) - scheduled 2026-03-15.
Billing: Issue one week service credit and confirm acceptance via billing ticket.
notes_for_sales_and_account: Customer was briefed directly on 2026-03-10; account requested SLA credit and weekly updates until patch lands. Sales/AM to confirm credit application and contract implications.
resolution_status_notes: Patch scheduled and hotfix validated in staging. Customer confirmed observed improvements after client backoff and hotfix. Ticket closed after customer sign-off on 2026-03-13.
